question: Which statement best describes Image component?
options: Import and use the `Image` component from `next/image`. It supports image sizing and optimization features in Next.js. It is like a picture frame that knows how to prepare its contents. Follow the current project’s Next.js version and configuration because supported options can change. For example, a fixed card ratio reserves space before a remote thumbnail has downloaded. In practice, reserve a thumbnail’s dimensions before a list response finishes loading.

Use `fill` when the parent element provides a sized container. The image then fills that area, often with `object-fit` controlling the crop. It is like placing a photo behind a fixed window. Ensure the parent has a size and test the crop at multiple screen widths. For example, a portrait headshot may need `object-position` so the face stays visible. In practice, check a portrait crop on both phone and desktop widths.

Width and height describe the image proportions and help reserve its space before loading. This reduces layout shift. It is like leaving a correctly sized frame on the wall before the picture arrives. Supply dimensions that match the source or use a layout pattern that preserves its ratio. For example, use `fill` only after the parent has a measurable position and size. In practice, give the parent a defined box when using a fill layout.

Alt text describes what an informative image contributes. Decorative images should use empty alt text so they can be skipped. It is like a caption that can be read aloud. Do not repeat nearby text unless it adds useful information about the image. For example, a decorative hero image can have empty alternative text when its message is already in nearby text. In practice, a decorative image can use empty alt text when nearby content carries the meaning.

Remote image hosts may need to be allowed in Next.js configuration. The setting limits which sources the image optimizer can fetch. It is like a guest list for an image service. Allow only the hosts the app needs, and verify remote images after deployment. For example, add a remote host narrowly instead of allowing every arbitrary image URL. In practice, allow only expected remote image hosts in configuration.
